scope: Historical health geography and the linked boards, councils and societies. This register reviews the repository evidence; it does not report newly acquired records or new legal-boundary findings.
requestStatus: All request wording is draft. No requests have been sent. Proposed custodians and record existence must be confirmed.

sources.title: Existing PGMaps BC Ministry of Health boundary snapshots
sources.note: Actual PGMaps layers, already simplified at 50 m (LHA), 75 m (HSDA), and 100 m (HA). Snapshot files do not declare an original historical vintage.

sources.title: BC Data Catalogue: Local Health Area Boundaries
sources.note: Official service describes its data as the 2022 boundary configuration; 2019 involved code/name updates and some health geography changes. The historical-code field was null in every downloaded feature.

sources.title: BC Data Catalogue: Health Service Delivery Area Boundaries
sources.note: Official metadata: 2022 configuration with minor digitizing improvements; previous boundaries from 2003.

sources.title: BC Data Catalogue: Health Authority Boundaries
sources.note: Official metadata describes 2022 configuration. These are contemporary geographic authorities, not the 1997 system.

sources.title: Ministry of Health 2019 LHA profile: old/new LHA code crosswalk
sources.note: Appendix C, printed pp 73–75 / PDF pp 75–77. Codes and names only; no claim of unchanged historic geometry.

sources.title: Auditor General 1997/98 Report 3: Exhibits 3–5
sources.note: Contemporaneous administrative maps for 11 boards, 34 council/related labels, and 7 societies. The vector artwork has no supplied geographic coordinates.

sources.title: Provincial Health Officer Annual Report 1998: Appendix G
sources.note: Printed G-2 distinguishes 20 analytical regions aggregated from LHAs from the new administrative system, and warns that regionalization involved boundary changes.

sources.title: Statistics Canada: matching January 2000 and June 2002 BC health-region boundaries
sources.note: The table identifies unchanged pairs for the two dated statistical systems. It does not certify their correspondence to 1997 administrative boundaries or today's polygons.

sources.title: Ministerial Order M432/1996: Regional Health Boards Regulation
sources.note: Legal descriptions for North Shore, Simon Fraser/Burnaby, and South Okanagan Similkameen.

sources.title: Ministerial Order M441/1996: regional board schedules
sources.note: Legal descriptions and amalgamating councils for Fraser Valley, South Fraser Valley, Thompson, Central Vancouver Island, Vancouver/Richmond, and Capital.

sources.title: Ministerial Order M444/1996: Northern Interior and North Okanagan
sources.note: Northern Interior legal description PDF pp 4–8; North Okanagan pp 9–12. The named constituent councils help select candidates but do not validate modern polygon edges.

sources.title: Ministerial Order M87/1997: community health council schedules
sources.note: Continues the community health councils and gives their boundary schedules; Appendix 21 retains the name 100 Mile House & District. The later rename is M225/1997.

sources.title: Ministerial Order M225/1997: South Cariboo council rename
sources.note: Made 23 May 1997; substitutes South Cariboo Community Health Council for 100 Mile House & District Community Health Council throughout B.C. Reg. 27/97. This establishes the name relationship, not unchanged modern geometry.

sources.title: Original Regional Health Boards Regulation, B.C. Reg. 293/2001
sources.note: Schedule A lists constituent institutions in the December 2001 amalgamations; it does not make their earlier boundaries identical to modern LHAs.

sources.title: Central Coast Land and Coastal Resource Management Plan: phase 1 socioeconomic assessment
sources.note: Describes the 1999 Cariboo health region as including Bella Coola Valley; supports that regional association rather than a measured polygon equivalence.

sources.title: Health Authority Performance Management ORCS 122352
sources.note: Prior repository review: PDF pp.51, 56–57; secondary 25440-40 describes society-amalgamation binders. Executive Records 102906 is a separate possible correspondence route, not a confirmed accession.

sources.title: Earlier health institutional records targets (21 October 2026)
sources.note: Existing retrieval specifications, not proof of current custody or completed transactions.

sources.title: M191/1997: Nisga’a council designation reference
sources.note: The statutory council is separately recorded; this does not resolve equivalence to the map label.

sources.title: M315/1997: North Okanagan rename
sources.note: Repository records made date 3 September 1997; OAG footnote gives 12 September. Deposit/effectiveness remains to be established.

usableNow.title: Original published maps and labels
usableNow.statement: Display four original map pages and all 52 administrative-map labels with their dates, legend numbers, credits and source links.
usableNow.limit: Publication artwork has no geographic coordinates. The 1997/98 maps are not certified as the final boundaries immediately before December 2001.

usableNow.title: Institutional name links
usableNow.statement: Link 51 labels to confirmed institution records. Preserve the Nisga’a source label separately.
usableNow.limit: Institutional identity does not establish territorial identity or the legal date of every merger.

usableNow.title: Written legal boundaries
usableNow.statement: Expose the indexed 1995 twenty-board definitions, 1996 board schedules and the published 1997 council schedules as research inputs.
usableNow.limit: These descriptions have not been reconstructed and checked against all intervening amendments. A link to a schedule is not a completed boundary audit.

usableNow.title: Modern comparison maps
usableNow.statement: Show 89 LHA, 16 HSDA and five geographic-authority polygons offline, with the proposed candidate for each source area.
usableNow.limit: All 52 candidates remain unverified historically. Current-data audit scores compare modern datasets only; the PGMaps snapshot date is undeclared.

usableNow.title: Dated statistical and code correspondences
usableNow.statement: Use the published statistical correspondence and 89-row old/new LHA crosswalk to explain candidate choices.
usableNow.limit: A statistical-region relationship or code translation does not prove an unchanged administrative boundary.

usableNow.title: Registered original drawings
usableNow.statement: Overlay the vector linework from all three administrative main maps on the modern layers. Compare 18 regional area drawings with modern LHA combinations and the best individual LHA, HSDA and HA features.
usableNow.limit: This is an exploratory three-control affine fit. Southern insets, the separate twenty-region statistical map, and all 34 council polygon scores remain unregistered or unscored as documented. Source-path assignments require independent review.

assumptions.title: Modern areas are a comparison canvas
assumptions.statement: A highlighted modern area is a working candidate selected from place names, constituent descriptions and dated correspondences. The new registered-drawing overlap is a cartographic comparison, not a verified legal-boundary overlap score.
assumptions.resolution: Reconstruct the dated legal territory or acquire authenticated historical GIS, then validate it independently.

assumptions.title: A name match does not settle scope
assumptions.statement: South Cariboo council follows the documented 100 Mile House rename. North West excludes Nisga’a in the source map. Northern Interior excludes the separately recorded Quesnel council in the proposed comparison. These findings constrain candidates without validating their edges.
assumptions.resolution: Retain these constraints while checking complete legal schedules and amendments.

assumptions.title: Dates must retain their meaning
assumptions.statement: Order-made, deposited, effective, publication and completed-transfer dates remain separate. The North Okanagan 3/12 September 1997 discrepancy and later coastal changes must stay visible.
assumptions.resolution: Locate the operative instruments and Gazette/deposit records; record each date with its meaning.

assumptions.title: Service territories can overlap
assumptions.statement: Council, board and society service geography must remain separate. A society’s service transfer is not established by its registry dissolution date or by a board consolidation schedule.
assumptions.resolution: Obtain the operative service-area schedules and completed transfer records before assigning dates or exclusive territories.

assumptions.title: Nisga’a identity remains open
assumptions.statement: The map’s Nisga’a Health Authority label is related geography, not a confirmed match to the statutory Nisga’a Community Health Council. Modern LHA 518 cannot settle the legal identity.
assumptions.resolution: Confirm the contemporaneous governing entity and service agreement with the relevant Nisga’a institutions and provincial records.

assumptions.title: Drawing alignment has local error
assumptions.statement: Three provincial corner controls per administrative main map determine an affine transform exactly. The held-out board-map Vancouver Island coastline has about 4.9 km median and 14.2 km 95th-percentile separation from the modern reference. That check includes coastline depiction differences and does not calibrate every page.
assumptions.resolution: Add independently identified physical control points and held-out checkpoints across each page. Review path-to-area assignments, offshore components and inset registration before treating a display candidate as a reconstructed territory.

workItems.title: Reconstruct the written board territories
workItems.question: Which modern candidate edges agree with the actual board descriptions?
workItems.recordsNeeded: The indexed M432/1996, M441/1996 and M444/1996 schedules, their referenced geographic units and dated base maps.
workItems.route: Original B.C. Reg. 293/2001 Schedule B now provides 44 written territories (11 boards and 33 councils). Reconcile these later descriptions with the original 1996/97 orders and amendments, then trace their dated survey, watershed and municipal references. M191/1997 supplies a related Nisga’a council definition, without settling the map identity.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Existing public legal sources; historical base-map custodians to be identified
workItems.completionEvidence: Clause-by-clause source table, dated geographic inputs, reproducible geometry and an independent review. Until then keep all modern candidates unverified.

workItems.title: Index and check the council boundary schedules
workItems.question: What territories do the council schedules actually describe?
workItems.recordsNeeded: M87/1997 appendices and relevant separate/amending instruments, including the Nisga’a council reference.
workItems.route: Original B.C. Reg. 293/2001 Schedule B now provides 44 written territories (11 boards and 33 councils). Reconcile these later descriptions with the original 1996/97 orders and amendments, then trace their dated survey, watershed and municipal references. M191/1997 supplies a related Nisga’a council definition, without settling the map identity.
workItems.completionEvidence: A sourced definition and dated amendment trail for every council/related label, or a specific missing-record entry.

workItems.title: Resolve the seven flagged candidate extents
workItems.question: Do the proposed aggregates include the complete historic territory and exclude neighbouring territory?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Schedules and contemporary local maps for Nelson/Area, Arrow Lakes/Upper Slocan, Bulkley Valley, Terrace/Area, Snow Country, Stikine and the North West society.
workItems.route: Start with published schedules and source-map notes. For each of the seven, document inclusion/exclusion of disputed subareas. Use the historical-map and society-territory requests for gaps.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Public legal sources first; Ministry, archives and successor-authority records as leads
workItems.dateRange: 1997/98 source map and relevant earlier/later amendments
workItems.completionEvidence: Individual decisions for all seven, with citations and unresolved clauses retained. Modern names alone cannot close an item.

workItems.title: Build a dated amendment and transfer chronology
workItems.question: Which source-map territories changed before or after consolidation?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Original amending orders, Gazette/deposit entries, the 2001 consolidation and 2002 coastal-transfer instruments; distinguish authorizations from completion.
workItems.route: Search BC Laws/Gazette and the existing health review first. Record made, deposit and operative dates separately; turn unrecovered instruments into precise requests.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Public legal publications; Ministry records staff for missing originals
workItems.completionEvidence: Per-area change log with exact operative wording and dates; preserve the North Okanagan discrepancy until deposit/effectiveness is resolved.

workItems.title: Improve and independently check the drawing registration
workItems.question: How much local distortion remains on each registered map?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Additional well-distributed physical control points, independently held-out checkpoints and reviewed coastal/area path assignments.
workItems.route: Review rectification-controls.json and the derived overlays. Use geographic landmarks, never the candidate administrative edges being tested. Refit with redundant controls and report residuals plus held-out error by page.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Existing original publication vectors and modern reference layers; obtain historical reference maps if needed
workItems.completionEvidence: Independent checkpoint errors by page, a documented transform/model comparison and reviewed source-path assignments; keep legal verification separate.

workItems.title: Review the 34 recovered council approximations
workItems.question: Can the registered council linework yield complete separately labelled polygons?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Original vector fill/stroke paths, printed legend numbers and explicit islands/holes/territory assignments.
workItems.route: All 34 source labels now have separate source-drawn working polygons, extracted without modern internal edges. Review the explicit seeds, local gap closure and offshore components in council-tracing.json; refine registration and check legal edges before certification.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Existing original publication vectors and modern reference layers; obtain historical reference maps if needed
workItems.completionEvidence: A reviewed path/seed crosswalk for all 34 labels, topology checks and extraction uncertainty; then run the same cartographic comparison.

workItems.title: Register the southern insets and twenty-region map
workItems.question: Can source detail support better comparisons in the Lower Mainland and southern Vancouver Island?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Separate control sets for each enlarged inset and the Statistics Canada twenty-region map; original page vectors and printed labels.
workItems.route: Treat each inset as a separate map with its own transform and geographic extent. Retain its provenance and reconcile it with the main map before using it for small regions. Independently register the statistical map without equating its regions to legal boards.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Existing original publication vectors and modern reference layers; obtain historical reference maps if needed
workItems.completionEvidence: Reviewed inset/statistical-map controls, independent checkpoints and explicit region identities; no mixed-scale coordinates in a single transform.

workItems.title: Obtain dated historical GIS or original cartography
workItems.question: Can actual historical administrative geometry and its provenance be recovered?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Existing 1995 twenty-board, 1997 board/council/society and pre/post-December 2001 boundary files; original cartographic source files, legends, metadata, version logs and historical reference-unit maps.
workItems.route: Ask Ministry of Health geography/data staff for existing releases and file inventories. Ask BC Archives about transferred cartographic records. If unpublished provincial records remain, scope an FOI to identified series, dates and file types.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Ministry of Health and BC Archives are proposed leads; no current custody or surviving GIS is confirmed
workItems.completionEvidence: Dated, attributed files with CRS/datum, valid-from/to, lineage and reuse terms; authenticate against legal schedules. An inventory or no-records reply does not verify boundaries.
workItems.requestText: Please identify existing electronic boundary datasets and original cartographic source files for BC regional health boards, community health councils and community health services societies, 1995–2002, especially the maps published as Exhibits 3–5 of the March 1998 Auditor General regionalization report and versions immediately before and after 12 December 2001. Please first provide a file/version inventory and identify any transferred archival accessions. For available files, seek native GIS/cartographic formats, associated legends, code tables, CRS/datum, effective dates, revision logs, source legal instruments and reuse conditions. This request seeks existing records, not creation of a new historical dataset.

workItems.title: Obtain society service-area schedules
workItems.question: What did each society’s jurisdiction/service territory include at the relevant date?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Executed service agreements, territorial schedules/maps and amendments for all seven societies, including Central Kootenay/Kootenay Boundary aliases, North West’s Nisga’a exclusion, Bella Coola and the mainland Central Coast.
workItems.route: Ask the Ministry and successor-authority records offices for public schedules and finding aids first. Investigate ORCS 122352 / 25440-40 for relevant agreements; its described amalgamation binders are a lead, not proof that service-area maps are held there. FOI only after identifying the provincial custodian and remaining records.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Ministry of Health, successor authorities and archival custodians; holdings unconfirmed
workItems.completionEvidence: Executed and dated territorial schedules for each society, with exclusions and amendments. A modern HSDA match or society name is insufficient.
workItems.requestText: Please identify existing service-area agreements, executed territorial schedules, maps and amendments for the seven community health services societies shown in Exhibit 5 of the March 1998 Auditor General report: East Kootenay, Central Kootenay (later Kootenay Boundary), Coast Garibaldi, Upper Island/Central Coast, Cariboo, North West and Peace Liard. The period is 1996–2002. Please include records explaining North West’s express Nisga’a exclusion and the Bella Coola/mainland Central Coast allocation. Please provide the file inventory/accession first, then the complete applicable schedules. ORCS 122352 / 25440-40 may be a relevant lead; please confirm applicability rather than assuming custody.

workItems.title: Confirm the Nisga’a map entity and territorial relationship
workItems.question: Which entity did the original map label identify, and what agreement defined its service area?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Contemporaneous governance/designation documents and service agreements linking or distinguishing the map label, statutory council and Nisga’a Valley Health Board; dated maps and transition records.
workItems.route: Review public Nisga’a institutional histories and provincial designation instruments. Request clarification and releasable records directly from the relevant Nisga’a institutions. Use provincial records access/FOI only for records held by a covered provincial body; do not presume Nisga’a institutions are subject to that process.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Relevant Nisga’a health/government institutions and Ministry of Health as proposed record holders; custody unconfirmed
workItems.dateRange: 1995–2001, including 1999 designation removal and 2000 governance transition
workItems.completionEvidence: A primary document explicitly connecting or distinguishing the named entities, with dated territorial terms. Preserve bodyId=null until identity is established.
workItems.requestText: We are researching the label “Nisga’a Health Authority”, number 32 in Exhibit 4 of the March 1998 Auditor General regionalization report, and its exclusion from North West in Exhibit 5. Could you identify publicly available or releasable 1995–2001 governance instruments, designation documents, service agreements and maps that explain its relationship to the Nisga’a Community Health Council and Nisga’a Valley Health Board? We seek the named legal/service entity and applicable dates and territory, especially around the 1999 designation change and 2000 governance transition. Please advise the appropriate records contact and any access or reuse conditions.

workItems.title: Recover the operative 2002 coastal-transfer record
workItems.question: Exactly which territory and services transferred, and on what effective date?
workItems.recordsNeeded: The operative legal/administrative transfer instruments, executed agreements, territorial annexes and maps for Bella Coola and Central Coast.
workItems.route: Search the public Gazette/orders and authority reports before requesting records. If the operative annexes remain missing, ask the Ministry and Interior, Vancouver Island/Island and Vancouver Coastal authority records offices; use FOI for identified unpublished provincial records.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Ministry of Health and the relevant successor health authorities; custody unconfirmed
workItems.completionEvidence: Operative effective date plus the actual territory/services described; today’s Vancouver Coastal polygon cannot serve as a December 2001 snapshot.
workItems.requestText: Please identify existing instruments, executed transfer agreements and territorial annexes/maps for the 2002 transfer of Bella Coola and Central Coast services/territory to Vancouver Coastal Health. The requested period is December 2001–December 2002. Please distinguish the decision/authorization date, operative transfer date and any staged service transfers, identify predecessor and receiving bodies, and provide complete geographic schedules and amendments. Please provide public references or file/accession identifiers first.

workItems.title: Keep statistical regions separate from administration
workItems.question: Which statistical relationships can be used without claiming legal equivalence?
workItems.recordsNeeded: PHO Appendix G, Statistics Canada January 2000/June 2002 correspondence and the published LHA code crosswalk.
workItems.route: Review the public tables; attach each correspondence to its stated vintage and evidence type. Use the statistical-data request only if downloadable historical geometry/metadata is needed.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Existing public PHO, Statistics Canada and Ministry publications
workItems.dateRange: 1998 report; January 2000/June 2002 statistical vintages; 2019 code crosswalk
workItems.completionEvidence: A source-backed statistical correspondence table whose fields and labels cannot be mistaken for historical legal boundary verification.

workItems.title: Obtain completed society and council/board transaction records
workItems.question: When were authorized amalgamations and society service transfers actually carried out?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Society executed asset/staff transfer and closing records; council/board completion resolutions, certificates and agreements. Use the existing named 43-council and seven-rural-board target index for predecessor work outside the 52 map labels.
workItems.route: Reuse the earlier request targets. For societies seek the ORCS 122352 / 25440-40 inventory and applicable registry filings. For council/board execution investigate separate ministry/executive correspondence (schedule 102906 is a lead). Request archives/direct access first, FOI for identified withheld/unpublished provincial files if needed.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Ministry records custodian, BC Archives, successor authorities and corporate registry; no accession confirmed
workItems.completionEvidence: Executed documents naming parties, transaction scope and effective/completion dates. Registry dissolution or conditional authority alone cannot date transfer of geography or services.
workItems.requestText: Please identify accessions and file indexes for Health Authority Performance Management ORCS 122352 / secondary 25440-40, “Society amalgamations with health authorities files”. For the seven rural community health services societies, seek complete executed asset/staff transfer agreements, schedules, consents and closing certificates, especially December 2001–February 2002. Separately, for council-to-board amalgamations authorized under the 1996 framework, identify completion resolutions, certificates and ministerial confirmation; Executive Records schedule 102906 is a possible lead, not a confirmed accession. Please keep society and council/board record searches distinct and identify the record custodian before expanding scope.

workItems.title: Locate historical statistical GIS and metadata
workItems.question: Are distributable January 2000/June 2002 statistical-region files available?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Original digital statistical-region boundaries, metadata, code lists and correspondence documentation for the two dated vintages.
workItems.route: Check Statistics Canada public historical downloads/archive and library holdings first. If unavailable, ask its geography/data service about existing files and access/reuse conditions. This is a data/library request before considering any formal access process.
workItems.likelyCustodian: Statistics Canada geography/data services and library/archive leads; availability unconfirmed
workItems.completionEvidence: Authentic dated statistical geometry with metadata and licence. It remains statistical geography even after acquisition.
workItems.requestText: Please advise whether existing BC health-region digital boundary files and accompanying code lists/metadata for January 2000 and June 2002 are publicly available or retrievable from archived holdings. The relevant published correspondence is Health Indicators table 4061979. Please provide original vintage definitions, coordinate system, correspondence notes and reuse conditions. We are keeping statistical regions distinct from administrative legal territories and do not request a newly reconstructed dataset.

workItems.title: Recover the PGMaps boundary snapshot provenance
workItems.question: What was the original snapshot’s download date and source revision?
workItems.recordsNeeded: Existing PGMaps export/download logs, source WFS/catalogue revision identifiers and original metadata sidecars.
workItems.route: Inspect PGMaps repository history and original file metadata first; ask its maintainer only if existing records do not settle provenance. FOI is not the first route for repository export history.
workItems.likelyCustodian: PGMaps repository/maintainer as a proposed source of export records
workItems.dateRange: Original snapshot creation period is unknown
workItems.completionEvidence: A documented acquisition/revision date or an explicit unresolved finding. The current-data audit cannot supply the missing historical snapshot date.
workItems.requestText: Please identify existing provenance records for the BCMoH LHA/HSDA/HA boundary snapshots served by PGMaps: original retrieval/export date, source dataset or WFS revision, transformation/simplification steps and metadata sidecars. A commit/upload date alone will be recorded as such, not automatically as the source boundary vintage.

assessments.assumption: The North Okanagan candidate combines Armstrong/Spallumcheen, Vernon, Enderby, Revelstoke and Salmon Arm. It spans today's Okanagan and Thompson Cariboo Shuswap HSDAs; either modern HSDA alone is the wrong extent.

The candidate uses Southern Okanagan, Penticton, Keremeos, Princeton, Central Okanagan and Summerland. Today's Okanagan HSDA also includes northern areas that belonged to the separate North Okanagan board.

The candidate uses Kamloops, North Thompson, Lillooet, South Cariboo LHA 148 and Merritt. The current Thompson Cariboo Shuswap HSDA includes additional Cariboo and Shuswap areas. Historical South Cariboo council around 100 Mile House is a different area.

assessments.candidateLabel: Documented historical relationship; modern polygon candidate
assessments.assumption: Fraser East is a strong comparison candidate: Statistics Canada explicitly equates January 2000 Fraser Valley with June 2002 Fraser Valley. This dated statistical correspondence still requires checking against the 1997 legal board boundary and modern changes.

assessments.candidateLabel: Documented historical relationship; modern polygon candidate
assessments.assumption: Fraser South is a strong comparison candidate supported by the January 2000-to-June 2002 statistical correspondence. Modern Surrey subdivisions do not establish unchanged historical board edges.

assessments.candidateLabel: Documented historical relationship; modern polygon candidate
assessments.assumption: The candidate combines Burnaby, New Westminster, Maple Ridge/Pitt Meadows and Tri-Cities. The 1997 board combined former Simon Fraser and Burnaby areas; Statistics Canada also documents this merged correspondence to the 2002 Simon Fraser HSDA.

Today's Central Vancouver Island HSDA is a useful geographic candidate, supported by its constituent place names. Its matching name is not proof that its legal edge equals the 1997 board; later Vancouver Island health boundaries changed.

Use Burns Lake, Nechako and Prince George as the candidate. Do not automatically use all of current Northern Interior HSDA 52: it also includes Quesnel, which was in the separate Cariboo area and had its own council.

assessments.candidateLabel: Documented historical relationship; modern polygon candidate
assessments.assumption: The candidate combines today's Vancouver and Richmond HSDAs. The historical institution amalgamated the predecessor Vancouver and Richmond regional health boards. Vancouver and Richmond remained separate labels in the 20-region statistical presentation. The 1996 legal schedule also incorporates specified electoral areas, so municipal names alone do not certify an exact match.

North Vancouver and West Vancouver/Bowen Island form the modern candidate. Today's North Shore/Coast Garibaldi HSDA is broader. The dated statistical correspondence combines North Shore with Coast Garibaldi; it does not independently validate LHA 331 and LHA 332 as the historical board boundary.

South Vancouver Island's Greater Victoria, Western Communities, Saanich Peninsula and Southern Gulf Islands provide the candidate. The legal 1996 schedule remains the authority for the historical edge.
Fernie is a place-based candidate for Elk Valley and South Country; the current LHA label does not reproduce the historic legal description.
Cranbrook is the direct place-name candidate; the 1997 schedule remains necessary for edge validation.
Kimberley is the direct place-name candidate; the 1997 schedule remains necessary for edge validation.
Windermere is the modern LHA covering the Columbia Valley candidate; the differing name is preserved.
Creston is the direct place-name candidate; district-level extent is not certified.
Nelson plus Kootenay Lake is a candidate for Nelson and Area; the inclusion of all Kootenay Lake needs checking against the legal schedule.
Castlegar is the direct place-name candidate; district-level extent is not certified.
Arrow Lakes is a starting candidate. Upper Slocan Valley is specifically named in the council and may not follow the modern Arrow Lakes LHA edge.
Trail is the place-name candidate for Greater Trail; greater-area extent remains unverified.
Grand Forks plus Kettle Valley is the Boundary-area candidate; this is an inferred grouping of modern LHAs.
Golden is the direct place-name candidate; the 1997 schedule remains necessary for edge validation.
This council was renamed from 100 Mile House & District. Use modern 100 Mile House LHA 144 as the candidate, not the differently located modern South Cariboo LHA 148.
Cariboo/Chilcotin is the geographic candidate for Central Cariboo Chilcotin; identical legal boundaries are not established.
Quesnel is the direct place-name candidate. Its current placement in Northern Interior HSDA does not place the former council inside the old Northern Interior board.
Bella Coola Valley is the place-name candidate. The source map and later transitional-authority identity are preserved as separate evidence.
Sunshine Coast is the direct place-name candidate; the 1997 schedule remains necessary for edge validation.
Powell River is the direct place-name candidate; the 1997 schedule remains necessary for edge validation.
Howe Sound is the modern geographic candidate for the Sea To Sky council; the changed name is not a boundary-equivalence assertion.
Comox Valley is the direct place-name candidate; the 1997 schedule remains necessary for edge validation.
Greater Campbell River plus Vancouver Island West is a candidate for Campbell River/Nootka; this is an inferred modern aggregation.
Vancouver Island North is the geographic candidate for Mount Waddington; the district name alone does not establish the historical edge.
Central Coast is the direct place-name candidate, including the mainland geography missing from a Vancouver-Island-only selection.
Peace River South is the modern place-name candidate for South Peace.
Peace River North is the modern place-name candidate for North Peace.
Fort Nelson is the modern geographic candidate for Fort Nelson-Liard.
Smithers is a starting candidate for Bulkley Valley. Coverage toward Houston and the old council's watershed limits must be checked; this is not a confirmed complete aggregation.
Upper Skeena is the direct place-name candidate; the 1997 schedule remains necessary for edge validation.
Terrace is a starting candidate; 'and Area' must be checked against the historic legal description, particularly neighbouring Nisga'a and Kitimat areas.
Kitimat is the place-name candidate; district-level extent is not certified.
Prince Rupert is the modern geographic candidate for North Coast; do not equate a present regional-district name with this council.
Haida Gwaii is the direct geographic candidate for Queen Charlotte Islands/Haida Gwaii; historical shore limits remain unverified.
This is related Nisga'a geography only. The map's 'Nisga'a Health Authority' identity is not confirmed equivalent to the repository's community-health-council record.
Snow Country LHA 511 and neighbouring Telegraph Creek LHA 519 are candidates requiring review. The historic council must not be assumed equal to either current area or their union solely from names.
Stikine LHA 516 is a starting candidate. Historical Stikine, Snow Country and Telegraph Creek subdivisions require legal-boundary comparison; names alone are insufficient.

assessments.candidateLabel: Documented historical relationship; modern polygon candidate
assessments.assumption: Today's East Kootenay HSDA is a strong candidate. Statistics Canada documents unchanged January 2000-to-June 2002 East Kootenay statistical geography. Society jurisdiction is related evidence, not a legal identity of all polygon edges.

assessments.candidateLabel: Documented historical relationship; modern polygon candidate
assessments.assumption: The source map calls this society Central Kootenay. Today's Kootenay Boundary HSDA is a strong candidate; Statistics Canada connects the older West Kootenay-Boundary statistical region with the 2002 Kootenay/Boundary HSDA.

assessments.candidateLabel: Documented historical relationship; modern polygon candidate
assessments.assumption: Sunshine Coast, Powell River and Howe Sound form the candidate. Do not use the whole present North Shore/Coast Garibaldi HSDA: North Shore was a separate board, and Bella Coola/Central Coast were associated with other former regions.

The candidate combines the current North Vancouver Island LHAs with Central Coast LHA 337. The former society's mainland Central Coast component makes today's North Vancouver Island HSDA alone incomplete.

The candidate combines 100 Mile House, Cariboo/Chilcotin, Quesnel and Bella Coola Valley. These now span Interior, Northern and Vancouver Coastal health authorities. A contemporary Cariboo-labelled area is not an adequate substitute.

The source society map explicitly excludes Nisga'a Health Authority. The modern candidate therefore uses Northwest LHAs except Nisga'a LHA 518; the whole Northwest HSDA 51 would incorrectly fill that exclusion. Using the modern Nisga'a edge to represent the historical exclusion remains unverified, and the old Northwest statistical region is not identical to this society's jurisdiction.

assessments.candidateLabel: Documented historical relationship; modern polygon candidate
assessments.assumption: Peace River South, Peace River North and Fort Nelson form the candidate. Statistics Canada documents the January 2000 Peace Liard to June 2002 Northeast statistical correspondence.
